title: The Man with the Twisted Lip
summary: A wife spots a strange man resembling her husband and asks Sherlock Holmes for help.
coverScene: A dimly lit gas-lit street at night with a man in a dark coat leaning against a brick wall, his face half-hidden by a raised collar and a twisted smile.

His name is Neville St. Clair.
He has a big house.
He has a family too.
He works in the city each day.
People say he is kind.
He leaves home early.
He comes home late.
One night, his woman sees something.
She goes to the city to buy things.

Mrs. St. Clair feels very bad.

Boone’s face looks bad.

They leave the house.
Mrs. St. Clair knows her man.
He would not have old things on.
She asks her friend Sherlock Holmes.
Holmes hears her story.

He sees something not right.

St. Clair goes home the next day.
He lives with his family again.
No one sees Hugh Boone after that.
The case is over.

sentences.text: In the year 1891, a man called Neville St. Clair lived in a large house near London.
He worked in the city and was a good and kind person.
Every morning, he left home early and came back late.
His family never worried about him because he always returned safely.
One evening, his wife went to the city to buy things for the house.
She saw something that surprised her a lot.
At a window of a small house, she saw a man who looked like her husband.
But he wore old clothes and his face seemed different.
The man moved his mouth in a strange way.
Mrs. St. Clair felt sure it was him.
When he saw her, he pulled back from the window quickly.
She felt very sad and worried.
Mrs. St. Clair called the police and told them what she saw.
They went to the house with her to check.
When they arrived, the man was not there.
Inside, they found only a poor man named Hugh Boone.
Boone had a strange mouth and sat in a chair.
He said he had not seen Mr. St. Clair that day.
The police did not believe Mrs. St. Clair.
They thought she made a mistake and left the house.
Mrs. St. Clair knew her husband would never wear such clothes.
She decided to ask her friend Sherlock Holmes for help.
Holmes listened to her story with care.
He agreed to look into the matter right away.
Holmes and his friend Dr. Watson went to the small house.
They found Boone still sitting in the same chair.
Holmes looked around the room and noticed something odd.
He asked Boone many questions, but Boone did not answer clearly.
Then Holmes quickly pulled at Boone’s hair.
The hair came off, and under it was Neville St. Clair’s face.
St. Clair admitted he had been living two lives.
He explained how it all started many years before.
He once wrote a piece about people who ask for money on the street.
To understand better, he tried it himself for one day.
He was surprised to make more money that way than at his job.
So he decided to keep doing it in secret.
He wore old clothes and made his face look different.
This way, no one would know who he really was.
But when his wife saw him, he knew his secret was in trouble.
He tried to stop her, but it was too late.
St. Clair promised to stop and return to his old life.
Holmes agreed not to tell the police if St. Clair kept his promise.
The next day, St. Clair went home to his family.
No one ever saw Hugh Boone again after that.
The case was solved, and everyone felt happy about the result.
Mrs. St. Clair was glad to have her husband back.
Holmes and Watson were pleased they could help.
St. Clair learned his lesson and never did it again.
His family was happy to have things return to normal.
They all lived together without any more secrets.
Mrs. St. Clair often thought about what had happened.
She was glad her husband was safe at home now.
Holmes told Watson that people sometimes do strange things for money.
But St. Clair had a good heart and would not do it again.
The police never found out about the secret.
They still thought Mrs. St. Clair had made a mistake.
St. Clair was careful never to go near that small house again.
He wanted to keep his family happy and safe.
His children never knew about his secret life.
They only knew their father as a good and kind man.
Years later, Mrs. St. Clair sometimes smiled when she remembered the day.
She was glad Holmes had helped them so quickly.
St. Clair worked hard at his job and was happy at home.
He never wanted to risk losing his family again.
Holmes and Watson often talked about the case.
It was one of the most unusual they had ever solved.
The small house where Boone sat was empty after that.
No one else ever lived there in the same way.
St. Clair’s life was back to normal, and he was glad.
He knew he had made a big mistake but was lucky to fix it.
